cited_entries: [L11] area=analyzer, generator: Types that come from a referenced assembly are deliberately not analysed and get no formatter from the compiling assembly. In `TypeCollector.CollectCore`, after the custom-formatter, enum and generic checks, a non-generic type whose symbol is metadata-only exits with a bare `if (type.Locations[0].IsInMetadata) { return; }` (TypeCollector.cs:367-370), so no MsgPack003/004/005 diagnostic and no generated formatter appear for it. The defining assembly owns validating and formatting its own types (rationale inferred: the code has no comment). A missing diagnostic or formatter for such a type is not a defect. (source: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:367)
details.plan: [L11] types from a referenced assembly get no formatter from the compiling assembly via TypeCollector.CollectCore; the new opt-in collector is a separate path and leaves the metadata-only exit at TypeCollector.cs:367-370 untouched.

title: Receipts/GeneratedFormatterReferencedTypeTests.cs: requirement test fails on base (2/2), passes on head (2/2); refutes 1 lens claim(s): requirement-tests-2

refutes.claim: The contractless mode here differs from the library's existing contractless behaviour in two ways. First, getter-only public members are silently dropped from serialization. Second, constructor parameters are never matched, so a class whose only constructor takes parameters is rejected with NoDeserializingConstructor. For an immutable type from a dependency-free library, 'contractless behaviour over public members' would therefore either lose data or not generate at all.
